title: FizzBuzz
problemStatement: Write a function `fizzBuzz(n)` that returns an array of strings from 1 to n where: for multiples of 3 use "Fizz", for multiples of 5 use "Buzz", for multiples of both 3 and 5 use "FizzBuzz", and otherwise the number itself as a string.
description: The output array has exactly n elements, one for each number from 1 to n in order.

examples.explanation: 3 is a multiple of 3 so it becomes Fizz; 5 is a multiple of 5 so it becomes Buzz.
15 is a multiple of both 3 and 5 so it becomes FizzBuzz.

explanation: Loop from 1 to n and append the correct string using modulo checks, checking divisibility by 15 first.

title: Palindrome Check
problemStatement: Write a function `isPalindrome(s)` that returns true if the string `s` reads the same forwards and backwards, and false otherwise.
description: The comparison is case-sensitive. Empty strings and single-character strings are palindromes.
constraints:
1 <= s.length <= 10^5
s contains only lowercase English letters
Time: O(N)
Space: O(1)

examples.explanation: hello reversed is olleh, which is different.

explanation: Compare characters from both ends moving towards the centre, or compare the string with its reverse.

title: Count Vowels and Consonants
problemStatement: Write a function `countVowelsConsonants(s)` that returns an array [vowels, consonants] with the number of vowels (a, e, i, o, u) and consonants in the string `s`.
description: The string contains only lowercase English letters. Vowels are a, e, i, o, u. Every other letter is a consonant.
constraints:
0 <= s.length <= 10^5
s contains only lowercase English letters
Time: O(N)
Space: O(1)
outputFormat: An array of two integers [vowels, consonants].

examples.explanation: Vowels are e, o; consonants are h, l, l.

explanation: Iterate through each character and increment the vowel counter if it is in {a, e, i, o, u}, otherwise increment the consonant counter.
